fix: When a series names its members ('the dorsal ..., the lateral sepals ...'), the member word must go into the position slot. Without it, the measure is wrongly said of every sepal.
reason: The 5-6 mm length is said of the lateral sepals only. The dorsal sepal is 3-4 mm long, so 'sepal 5-6 mm long' without 'lateral' is false.
The flowering stem is up to 8 cm tall. Height fits an erect stem, and the flowering-stage slot matches 'flowering stem'.

The flowers range from white to lilac, mauve or violet. All three of the second colours fall under the purple backbone class (FLOPO_0988008), so white to purple (FLOPO_0988009 to FLOPO_0988008) is right.

target: style branch (no PO class; the style PO_0009074 is the container)
fix: 'branches' after 'style ... surmonté de' means style branches (arms of the style), not shoot branches. PO_0025073 is a shoot-axis branch. 'branche(s)' should only map to PO_0025073 when the whole is a stem or shoot.
reason: The 3 short branches belong to the style, each with 2 stigmas. They are not shoot branches.
The involucral bracts are long sheathed, so bract + sheathing is right.
Styles usually 5; the count of 5 is right.
Subequal glumes = approximately equal in size. This matches the size + equal + approximately pattern.

target: base of the leaflet (lateral leaflets) + asymmetrical (PATO_0000616)
fix: In 'base ... oblique' / 'that of lateral ones oblique', 'that' points back to the base. Oblique here is said of the base and means an asymmetric base (a shape). It is not the orientation of the whole leaflet.
reason: The flora says the base of the lateral leaflets is oblique, not the leaflet as a whole. Oblique orientation (PATO_0002481) is also the wrong meaning: an oblique base is an asymmetrical base.
The hypanthium is about 12 mm in diameter in fruit. The fruit development stage (PO_0001002) is right.
The stem leaves typically number more than 20 (range 18-55), so more than 20 leaves is what the flora says.
The stamens are shorter than the petals.
A 3-5-flowered cyme = 3-5 flowers in the inflorescence.

fix: In 'X with reddish hairs', the colour belongs to the hairs. It should go on the trichome, with X as the container, not on X.
reason: The hairs are reddish, not the rhizome.
The sepals are white pubescent on the abaxial side, so sepal abaxial epidermis + pubescent is right.
The rhizomes are scaly.
The fruiting pedicel is reddish when fresh. The 'when fresh' condition slot is kept.
Shrubs or small trees = shrub habit or tree habit, given as alternatives.

target: petal limb (blade of a clawed petal; no PO class, so a FLOPO anatomy class or the petal apex region is needed)
fix: With 'clawed ... with suborbicular limb', the shape belongs to the limb. Read as petal + orbicular, it describes the whole clawed petal, which is false.
reason: The flora calls the limb suborbicular, not the whole petal. The petal is clawed.

fix: In a parenthetical about 'the varnish, in age, becoming ...', the quality belongs to the varnish, a secretion on the surface. It does not belong to the lamina.
reason: The varnish on the leaf faces becomes whitish and opaque with age. The leaf blade itself does not become opaque.
The stigmas are equal in length to the petals (ratio 1).
Branches without thorns = thorns absent. The branch could be added as the container, but the statement is true as given.
The fruit apex is ± acuminate. 'Acuminate' already refers to the apex, and approximately covers the ±.
The bract is 1-nerved = 1 vein (vascular bundle, synonym 'vein') in the bract.
The leaf blade is glabrous adaxially.
The calyx is campanulate-globose, a shape between campanulate and globose. That matches the continuum reading.

target: leaflet adaxial side (adaxial epidermis) + pubescent; the abaxial side is sericeous
fix: In 'Q1 ... abaxially, Q2 adaxially', the place word comes after its quality. Here 'abaxially' closes the first clause; it does not open the second. Place words should attach to the quality that comes before them.
reason: The appressed pubescence is on the upper (adaxial) side. The lower (abaxial) side is sericeous with brownish hairs.
The base of the leaf blade is cuneate and attenuate into the petiole.
Seeds many = seeds present, with the count word 'many'.
The leaflets are 7-14 cm long.
The leaflet apex is never mucronate, so negated mucronate is right. The apex is implied by the word.
